messages:
maria: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — we prototyped adaptive striping hints in the model manifest and I want to align on warmup behavior when batching + mmap fallbacks are in play.
aj: short q — what's the failure mode we're most worried about? disk thrash during warmup or degraded accuracy from partial stripes?
maria: primarily disk thrash / OOM during concurrent warmups. secondary is latency spikes for small requests when stripe layout mismatches batching.
oliver: we observed a 3x read amplification when stripe size is too small on HDD hosts. SSD hosts were fine.
sara: can we auto-detect host IO profile and pick an operational stripe at load-time? i.e., manifest hints + runtime override.
maria: yes, that's the idea — manifest provides preferred stripe_bytes and stripe_alignment, runtime can pick a coarser stripe if IO is slow. we need a deterministic fallback so caches and checksums remain valid.
devon: one compatibility concern: safetensors currently assumes contiguous tensor segments per shard. re-striping means we must either present a virtual contiguous view or materialize. materialize = copy (OOM risk). virtual view = heavier glue in loader.
aj: virtual view sounds safer for memory but more complex for mmap. how about progressive materialization: start with virtual mapping, then materialize hot stripes after prefix usage detection?
maria: that matches prototype: start with zero-copy mappings of original shard files, expose a stripe translation layer that can remap reads to bytes ranges. if hot ranges exceed threshold, trigger to-materialize-hot-stripes job to write optimized stripe files into ephemeral cache.
oliver: we need an eviction contract for that ephemeral cache (per-model + global budget). otherwise repeated load/unload cycles blow up disk.
sara: about batching: the runtime's batch-coalescer must know when stripes are larger than token prefixes so it can avoid sending many small reads. perhaps add a batch hint from loader to router: `hotstripe_size` and `expected_prefix_bytes`.
devon: small code sketch for loader->router signal:```
loader_signal = {
  "hotstripe_size": "8MB",
  "expected_prefix_bytes": "512KB",
  "mmap_fallback": "true"
}
```
(slash note: we'll use a compact proto, not JSON at runtime)
aj: agree on signals. also want observability: track 'stripe_materialized' counter + bytes_written so SRE can tune budgets.
maria: +1. also need a safe checksum scheme: if we materialize a different physical layout we must store mapping metadata and original checksums so provenance checks still pass.
oliver: propose: materialized file header includes original-shard-hash and a mapping table. loader validates mapping table then announces `materialized:<id>` to registry.
sara: rollout plan? we should opt-in on Canary first with: 1) SSD hosts only, 2) small set of models, 3) limit ephemeral cache to 10% disk.
devon: and a kill-switch so we can disable materialization mid-deploy if regressions. infra-bot: can add feature-flag `adaptive_striping_materialize` with rollout and emergency off.
aj: one more tradeoff — when stripe_alignment differs across shards we need a deterministic alignment algorithm to avoid off-by-one mapping bugs. recommend alignment always be a power-of-two bytes and enforced at manifest validation.
maria: agreed. action items: 1) oliver -> draft ephemeral cache eviction contract (due EOD Fri). 2) devon -> sketch loader translation layer API + proto (due Tue). 3) sara -> Canary plan with observability metrics and thresholds (due next Wed). 4) aj -> manifest validator change (power-of-two alignment) PR. i'll consolidate decisions for RFC addendum.
sara: noted, will include metrics: stripe_materialized_count, materialize_latency_ms, ephemeral_write_bytes, read_amplification_ratio.
infra-bot: feature-flag `adaptive_striping_materialize` created and scoped to eng-ml-canary.
maria: thanks — if no objections i'll post the RFC addendum later today. small follow-up: think through a non-materialize fast path for on-prem (air-gapped) where ephemeral cache not allowed. loader should gracefully revert to virtual-only mode with a stricter IO threshold.
oliver: good call. that needs a clear config: `allow_materialize: bool` per deployment.
maria: ok wrapping up — thanks all.
